Here is the complete, ordered list of every check that must pass before the pipeline is allowed to change a deployment. The checks come from three layers: the **pipeline job ordering** (`.gitlab-ci.yml`), the **rollback script** (`scripts/ci_rollback.py`), and the **safety gate** (`backend/app/services/safety.py`).

---

## Layer 1 — Pipeline job ordering (`.gitlab-ci.yml`)

These are structural gates enforced by GitLab CI job dependencies and `when: manual` triggers. A later job cannot start unless all its `needs:` predecessors succeeded.

| # | Check | File & line |
|---|-------|-------------|
| 1 | **Attribution guard passes** — scans every tracked file and every commit message in the range for AI attribution footers/trailers. Pipeline fails immediately if any are found. | `.gitlab-ci.yml` `attribution-guard` job (stage `verify`) |
| 2 | **Workload image builds and its immutable digest is captured** — the image must push successfully and `docker image inspect` must resolve a real digest (not the tag itself); otherwise the job exits 1. | `.gitlab-ci.yml` `build:workload-image` job (stage `build`) |
| 3 | **Healthy deployment passes its own health gate** — `ci_release.py probe` is run with `--expect-healthy` against the v1 release; the job fails if the service is not healthy, and the baseline window artifact is only written on success. | `.gitlab-ci.yml` `deploy:staging` job (stage `deploy`) |
| 4 | **Regression is real — the detector must fire** — `ci_incident.py regress` runs the real detector; if no regression is detected the job fails and no incident bundle is written, so no incident can be manufactured from a healthy release. | `.gitlab-ci.yml` `deploy:regressed` job (`when: manual`, stage `deploy`) |
| 5 | **A human explicitly starts the approval job** — `approval:grant` is `when: manual`, so a real GitLab user must click "Run" and their `GITLAB_USER_LOGIN` is recorded in the approval artifact. | `.gitlab-ci.yml` `approval:grant` job (stage `operate`) |
| 6 | **A human explicitly starts the rollback job** — `rollback:managed` is also `when: manual`; it only becomes available after `approval:grant` succeeds. | `.gitlab-ci.yml` `rollback:managed` job (stage `operate`) |

---

## Layer 2 — Rollback script pre-flight (`scripts/ci_rollback.py`)

These checks run inside the `rollback:managed` job before any deployment change is made.

| # | Check | File & line |
|---|-------|-------------|
| 7 | **Incident bundle exists on disk** — if the bundle file is absent the script prints an error and returns `EXIT_FAILED` without touching anything. | `scripts/ci_rollback.py` `main()`, ~line 196 |
| 8 | **Idempotency ledger is readable** — if `rollback-state.json` exists but is corrupt JSON, the script raises `SystemExit` with a refusal message; a corrupt ledger is never treated as "no prior executions". | `scripts/ci_rollback.py` `load_state()`, ~line 155 |
| 9 | **Safety gate allows the rollback** (see Layer 3 below) — `evaluate_gate()` is called and if `decision.allowed` is `False` the script writes the record and returns `EXIT_REFUSED` without deploying. | `scripts/ci_rollback.py` `main()`, ~line 218 |
| 10 | **`--dry-run` short-circuit** — if `ROLLBACK_DRY_RUN=1` the script stops here and changes nothing, even though the gate passed. | `scripts/ci_rollback.py` `main()`, ~line 224 |
| 11 | **`--image` is supplied** — without an image reference there is no artifact to deploy; the script returns `EXIT_FAILED`. | `scripts/ci_rollback.py` `main()`, ~line 229 |
| 12 | **Image digest matches the approved target digest** — `ci_release.image_digest()` resolves the *actual* digest of the image about to be deployed and `verify_target_identity()` requires it to equal the digest recorded in the bundle. An unknown digest on either side is refused. | `scripts/ci_rollback.py` `verify_target_identity()`, ~line 130; called in `main()` ~line 234 |

---

## Layer 3 — `SafetyGate.check()` (`backend/app/services/safety.py`)

All checks are evaluated independently; **every** failing check is a veto, and the rollback is allowed only when **all** pass.

| # | Check code | What it verifies | File & line |
|---|-----------|-----------------|-------------|
| 13 | `ACTION_IS_ROLLBACK` | The proposed action is literally `"rollback"` — `"hold"` and `"escalate"` must never trigger a deployment change. | `safety.py` ~line 72 |
| 14 | `ENVIRONMENT_ALLOWLISTED` | The target environment is in the operator-configured allowlist (`demo-staging` by default). | `safety.py` ~line 78 |
| 15 | `PHASE1_ENVIRONMENT_ALLOWLISTED` | The target environment is also in the protected-environments set (a second, independent allowlist check). | `safety.py` ~line 83 |
| 16 | `PROPOSAL_ENVIRONMENT_MATCHES` | The environment named in the proposal matches the environment the job is actually running against. | `safety.py` ~line 89 |
| 17 | `CURRENT_RELEASE_KNOWN` | The currently deployed release is known; without it, target identity and no-op detection are guesses. | `safety.py` ~line 95 |
| 18 | `TARGET_RELEASE_KNOWN` | The rollback target exists as an observed release. | `safety.py` ~line 101 |
| 19 | `TARGET_IS_KNOWN_GOOD` | The target release has been verified healthy by this system (`known_good=True`). | `safety.py` ~line 106 |
| 20 | `TARGET_DIFFERS_FROM_CURRENT` | The target is not the release already deployed (prevents a no-op rollback). | `safety.py` ~line 111 |
| 21 | `TARGET_ENVIRONMENT_MATCHES` | The target release's recorded environment matches the request environment. | `safety.py` ~line 118 |
| 22 | `MIGRATION_COMPATIBLE` *(conditional)* | If the proposal sets `requires_migration=True`, the target release must have `migration_compatible=True`; unknown is refused. | `safety.py` ~line 124 |
| 23 | `APPROVAL_PRESENT` | An approval record is present in the bundle. | `safety.py` ~line 131 |
| 24 | `APPROVAL_ACTOR_IS_HUMAN` | The approval actor is not in the `NON_HUMAN_ACTORS` denylist (bots, CI tokens, etc.). | `safety.py` ~line 135 |
| 25 | `APPROVAL_GRANTED` | The approval decision is `APPROVED`, not `DENIED` or pending. | `safety.py` ~line 141 |
| 26 | `APPROVAL_IN_SCOPE` | The approval's `proposal_hash` matches the current proposal's hash — the proposal cannot have changed after approval. | `safety.py` ~line 146 |
| 27 | `APPROVAL_ENVIRONMENT_MATCHES` | The approval was granted for the same environment being targeted. | `safety.py` ~line 152 |
| 28 | `APPROVAL_NOT_EXPIRED` | The approval has not passed its `expires_at` timestamp. | `safety.py` ~line 157 |
| 29 | `APPROVAL_WITHIN_MAX_AGE` | The approval's validity window does not exceed the policy maximum (900 s by default). | `safety.py` ~line 162 |
| 30 | `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_PRESENT` | A non-empty idempotency key is present (in the bundle or passed via `--idempotency-key`). | `safety.py` ~line 170 |
| 31 | `NOT_ALREADY_EXECUTED` | The idempotency key has not already been consumed by a prior rollback execution. | `safety.py` ~line 175 |

---

### Summary

There are **31 ordered checks** across three layers. The pipeline enforces structural ordering (jobs 1–6); the rollback script adds pre-flight guards (7–12); and the `SafetyGate` evaluates all 19 named checks (13–31) atomically, reporting every veto rather than stopping at the first. A deployment change only happens when every single one passes.

# RollbackIQ CI.
#
# Stages carry the real lifecycle: the attribution guard, a real image build,
# a real deployment that is only accepted when it passes a health gate, a
# deliberate regression, a human approval, a safety-gated rollback, and an
# independent verification of recovery.
#
# Two properties are deliberate and worth stating because they are easy to get
# wrong:
#
#   * GitLab jobs run on separate ephemeral runners, so a container started in
#     one job does not exist in the next. State that must survive travels as
#     job artifacts, and each job re-establishes the deployment it needs. The
#     incident bundle, the approval and the rollback evidence are all artifacts.
#   * The rollback job does not decide for itself. It runs the control plane's
#     SafetyGate over the incident bundle, so the rules that protect the
#     rollback are the same ones the test suite exercises. Any veto refuses.
#
# The `demo-staging` environment is an isolated demo target. Nothing here is
# wired to a customer system, and no job restores deleted data.

stages:
  - verify
  - build
  - deploy
  - operate

variables:
  # One image serves both releases; a release is a set of deployment inputs, not
  # a different build. That is what makes "roll back" a change of inputs.
  WORKLOAD_IMAGE: "$CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE/workload:$CI_COMMIT_SHA"
  DEPLOY_ENV: "demo-staging"
  DOCKER_NETWORK: "rollbackiq-ci"
  WORKLOAD_CONTAINER: "rollbackiq-workload"

# Shared docker-in-docker setup for the jobs that run the workload.
.docker-dind:
  image: docker:27
  services:
    - docker:27-dind
  variables:
    DOCKER_HOST: tcp://docker:2376
    DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR: "/certs"
    DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY: "1"
    DOCKER_CERT_PATH: "/certs/client"
    DOCKER_DRIVER: overlay2
  before_script:
    - apk add --no-cache python3 py3-pip
    # The release, incident and rollback scripts use the control plane's typed
    # models and the verifier, so the job installs the same requirements.
    - pip install --break-system-packages --quiet -r backend/requirements.txt

# The control-plane scripts need only Python; this keeps the approval job light.
.python:
  image: python:3.12-slim
  before_script:
    - pip install --quiet --no-cache-dir -r backend/requirements.txt

# Fails the pipeline if any committed file or commit message contains an AI
# attribution footer, trailer or assistant signature (AGENTS.md section 10).
# Uses the same scanner as the local Git hooks, so there is one rule to update.
attribution-guard:
  stage: verify
  image: alpine:3.20
  variables:
    GIT_DEPTH: "0"
  before_script:
    - apk add --no-cache bash grep git coreutils
  script:
    - echo "Scanning tracked and untracked files for attribution footers"
    - bash scripts/check_no_attribution.sh files
    - |
      base="${CI_MERGE_REQUEST_DIFF_BASE_SHA:-${CI_COMMIT_BEFORE_SHA:-}}"
      case "$base" in
        ""|0000000000000000000000000000000000000000) base="" ;;
      esac
      if [ -n "$base" ]; then
        echo "Scanning commit messages in $base..$CI_COMMIT_SHA"
        bash scripts/check_no_attribution.sh range "$base..$CI_COMMIT_SHA"
      else
        echo "Scanning commit messages reachable from $CI_COMMIT_SHA"
        bash scripts/check_no_attribution.sh range "$CI_COMMIT_SHA"
      fi

# Builds the workload image and publishes its immutable digest. The digest is
# the identity a rollback is allowed to target, so it is captured here and
# passed forward as an artifact rather than re-derived from a moving tag.
build:workload-image:
  stage: build
  extends: .docker-dind
  script:
    - docker build --build-arg RELEASE_VERSION=v1 -t "$WORKLOAD_IMAGE" ./demo/service
    - docker push "$WORKLOAD_IMAGE"
    - |
      DIGEST=$(docker image inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' "$WORKLOAD_IMAGE" | sed 's/.*@//')
      if [ -z "$DIGEST" ] || [ "$DIGEST" = "$WORKLOAD_IMAGE" ]; then
        echo "could not resolve an immutable digest for $WORKLOAD_IMAGE" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      printf '%s\n' "$DIGEST" > image-digest.txt
      echo "workload image digest: $DIGEST"
